files.title: Workflow 3.5.1.1 · Run a STRIDE Session
files.body:
# Workflow 3.5.1.1 · Run a STRIDE Session

Draw the design's trust boundaries, ask at each crossing whether it can be spoofed, tampered with, repudiated, disclosed, denied or elevated, and choose controls that fail closed.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-5-1-1-stride.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-5-1-1-run-stride`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-5-1-1-stride
title: "Run a STRIDE Session"
owner: "Security architect"
inputs:
  - "docs/system-design.md"
  - "docs/data-lineage.md"
  - "docs/architecture-description.md"
preconditions:
  - "System design drafted"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Draw the DFD & trust boundaries"
    owner: "Security architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-1-1-s1-draw-the-dfd-and-trust-boundaries
    skills: [data-flow-diagramming, trust-boundary]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/threat-model.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Walk STRIDE per crossing"
    owner: "Security architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-1-1-s2-walk-stride-per-crossing
    skills: [stride, misuse-cases, threat-modelling]
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, privacy-reviewer]
    output: "docs/threat-model.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Rate threats & choose controls"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-1-1-s3-rate-threats-and-choose-controls
    skills: [attack-trees]
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/threat-model.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "No acceptable control → stop the feature": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Check controls fail closed; record accepted threats"
    owner: "Security architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-1-1-s4-check-controls-fail-closed-record-accepted-threats
    reviewers: [security-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/threat-model.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Every high threat controlled or accepted?"
    owner: "Security"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Security decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Uncontrolled high threat → new control": s3
      "Residual high risk → risk owner": authority
gate: "Threat model review"
criteria:
  - "Every crossing walked"
  - "Failure mode per control"
checks:
  - "Security peer review"
on_failure:
  - "Label each control and re-rate the threat"
rework: "Uncontrolled high threat → choose a control and re-rate"
outputs:
  - "docs/threat-model.md"
  - "docs/threat-model.md"
handoff: "Threat model & data-flow diagram → 3.5.2 Define Security Requirements & Controls"
learning:
  - "Threats found later in VERIFY or OPERATE — learning log"
```

files.title: Workflow 3.5.3.1 · Screen & Assess Privacy Impact
files.body:
# Workflow 3.5.3.1 · Screen & Assess Privacy Impact

Screen the processing against Article 35, then assess necessity, proportionality and risks to individuals, choose measures and sign off the residual risk.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-5-3-1-dpia.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-5-3-1-run-dpia`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-5-3-1-dpia
title: "Screen & Assess Privacy Impact"
owner: "Privacy officer"
inputs:
  - "docs/data-lineage.md"
  - "docs/data-inventory.md"
preconditions:
  - "Lineage drafted"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Screen against Article 35"
    owner: "Privacy officer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-3-1-s1-screen-against-article-35
    skills: [data-classification]
    reviewers: [privacy-reviewer, compliance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dpia.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Personal data processed?"
    owner: "Privacy officer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Privacy officer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s2
      "No personal data → screening record only": s4
  - id: s2
    do: "Describe processing & assess necessity"
    owner: "Data owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-3-1-s2-describe-processing-and-assess-necessity
    skills: [data-contract]
    reviewers: [privacy-reviewer, legal-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dpia.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Assess risks & choose measures"
    owner: "Privacy officer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-3-1-s3-assess-risks-and-choose-measures
    skills: [linddun, threat-modelling]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, security-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dpia.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d2
    decision: "Residual risk acceptable?"
    owner: "Privacy officer"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Privacy officer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Too high → more measures": s3
      "High residual → supervisory authority": authority
      "Unlawful → stop that processing": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Sign off & record"
    owner: "Privacy officer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-5-3-1-s4-sign-off-and-record
    reviewers: [compliance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/dpia.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Privacy review"
criteria:
  - "Screening recorded"
  - "Measure per risk"
checks:
  - "Privacy officer review"
on_failure:
  - "Treat findings as defects with owners; re-assess before release"
rework: "Residual risk too high → add measures and re-assess"
outputs:
  - "docs/dpia.md"
  - "docs/dpia.md"
handoff: "Privacy impact assessment → 3.5.4 Assess Third-Party Risk and 3.6.4 Design Readiness"
learning:
  - "Privacy issues found after release — learning log"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 3.6.2.1 · Write Quality-Attribute Scenarios

Write each driver as a six-part scenario, set its measure from data, choose how it will be verified and trace it.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-6-2-1-nfr-scenarios.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-6-2-1-run-nfr-scenarios`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-6-2-1-nfr-scenarios
title: "Write Quality-Attribute Scenarios"
owner: "Architect"
inputs:
  - "docs/utility-tree.md"
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
preconditions:
  - "Drivers ranked"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Write the six parts per driver"
    owner: "Architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-2-1-s1-write-the-six-parts-per-driver
    skills: [quality-attribute-scenario, attribute-driven-design]

    output: "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Need withdrawn": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Set measures from data & the load model"
    owner: "Architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-2-1-s2-set-measures-from-data-and-the-load-model
    skills: [load-model]

  - id: s3

    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-2-1-s3-choose-the-verification-method

    checkpoint: review-at-end

    decision: "Measurable, verifiable, affordable?"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 3.6.3.1 · Analyse Trade-offs

Map each decision to the scenarios it moves, find sensitivity and trade-off points, and define fitness functions for the key scenarios.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-6-3-1-trade-offs.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-6-3-1-run-trade-offs`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-6-3-1-trade-offs
title: "Analyse Trade-offs"
owner: "Architect"
inputs:
  - "docs/qa-scenarios.md"
  - "docs/adr.md"
  - "docs/system-design.md"
preconditions:
  - "Scenarios written"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Map decisions to scenarios"
    owner: "Architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-3-1-s1-map-decisions-to-scenarios
    skills: [utility-tree, attribute-driven-design]

    output: "docs/tradeoff-analysis.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Find sensitivity & trade-off points"
    owner: "Architect"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-3-1-s2-find-sensitivity-and-trade-off-points
    skills: [failure-mode-analysis, circuit-breaker]
    reviewers: [performance-reviewer, ai-reviewer, reliability-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/tradeoff-analysis.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Define fitness functions"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-3-1-s3-define-fitness-functions
    skills: [fitness-function]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, devops-reviewer]
    output: "docs/tradeoff-analysis.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end

    decision: "Top scenarios met with accepted trade-offs?"

    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"

  - "Trade-offs that surprised the team — learning log"
```

# Workflow 3.6.4.1 · Hold the Design Readiness Review

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-6-4-1-readiness.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-6-4-1-run-readiness`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-6-4-1-readiness
title: "Hold the Design Readiness Review"
owner: "Architect"
inputs:

  - "docs/threat-model.md"

preconditions:
```

files.body:
# Workflow 3.6.4.2 · Run the Ready Gate on a Story

Run the eight conditions — purpose, requirements, acceptance criteria, dependencies, architecture impact, design, testability, size — on one story, record any failure with its correction, and recheck only what changed.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-6-4-2-ready-gate.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-6-4-2-run-ready-gate`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-6-4-2-ready-gate
title: "Run the Ready Gate on a Story"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
  - "docs/definition-of-ready.md"
  - "docs/impact-check.md"
  - "docs/ui-spec.md"
preconditions:
  - "Story sliced by behaviour with acceptance criteria"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Check purpose, requirements & criteria (1–3)"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-4-2-s1-check-purpose-requirements-and-criteria-1-3
    skills: [invest, specification-by-example]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/backlog-item.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Check dependencies, impact & design (4–6)"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-4-2-s2-check-dependencies-impact-and-design-4-6
    skills: [definition-of-ready, design-review]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer, ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/ready-gate-result.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Dependency without an owner → delivery lead": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Check testability & size (7–8)"
    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-4-2-s3-check-testability-and-size-7-8
    skills: [three-amigos]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, engineering-reviewer, researcher]
    output: "docs/ready-gate-result.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "All eight conditions met?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Failed condition → its return point; recheck only what changed": s1
      "Story no longer needed → remove": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Record result, failures & corrections"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

criteria:
  - "Eight conditions met"
  - "Approver is not an author"
checks:
  - "Evidence per condition"
on_failure:
  - "Approval tied to this exact version; any change re-opens the gate"
  - "Named approver who is not an author"
rework: "Failed condition → correct at its return point; recheck that condition and anything the correction touched"
outputs:
  - "docs/ready-gate-result.md"
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
handoff: "Ready story → product backlog → BUILD sprint planning"
learning:
  - "Which condition fails most often — learning log"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act III DESIGN · Scale: Product team. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
DESIGN is part of the **Discovery track** — Are we building the right thing? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## DESIGN: Decide the experience, domain, architecture, data and safeguards — to the depth the risk demands — so that building is low-risk and traceable.
- **3.1 Experience Design** — gate: Experience Review. Produces: UX flows, Validated prototype, Usability findings, UI specification, State matrix, Accessibility checklist.
- **3.2 Domain Modelling** — gate: Domain Model Review. Produces: Ubiquitous language glossary, Context map, Domain model, Invariant catalogue.
- **3.3 Architecture Definition** — gate: Architecture Baseline. Produces: Architecture Impact Check, System design, ADRs, Architecture views, Architecture baseline.
- **3.4 Data Design** — gate: Data Design Review. Produces: Data model, Data ownership table, Data lineage map, Data classification & retention schedule, Migration plan.
- **3.5 Security & Privacy by Design** — gate: Security & Privacy Review. Produces: Threat model, Security requirements, Privacy impact assessment, Vendor security assessment.
- **3.6 Quality Attribute Specification** — gate: Design Readiness. Produces: Ranked quality drivers, Quality-attribute scenarios, Trade-off analysis, Fitness functions, Design readiness record, Design pack, Ready stories, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Design Readiness** — decided by: The architect decides design readiness; the product owner approves Ready stories; the design authority settles cross-team conflicts; no one approves what they authored..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: UXF → PRT → UIS → DOM → ARC → ADR → DAT → THR → DPIA → QAS → DRR → STY → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `design-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Product team
Write for a product trio and a delivery team. Use our shared templates, make outputs ready to drop into the backlog or repository, and flag anything that needs the team's refinement.
Access: Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.

# Guardrails & hooks — Design

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Product team
- Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
- Watch for: Each person's agent producing inconsistent artifacts — use the shared templates
- Watch for: Discovery and delivery drifting apart

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit

- No story enters a sprint without passing the Ready Gate
- Reviewers never approve what they authored

# Workflow 3.1.1.1 · Map the To-Be Flows

Turn the release's requirements and today's workflow into agreed to-be flows and wireframes, including what happens when things fail.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-1-1-1-map-flows.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-1-1-1-run-map-flows`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-1-1-1-map-flows
title: "Map the To-Be Flows"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/workflow-maps.md"
  - "docs/jtbd.md"
preconditions:
  - "Requirements baseline approved"
  - "Release scope known from the roadmap"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Select jobs & requirements for the release"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s1-select-jobs-and-requirements-for-the-release
    skills: [double-diamond]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Policy change needed → process owner": authority
      "No user-facing change": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Analyse today's task"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s2-analyse-today-s-task
    skills: [task-analysis, journey-mapping, service-blueprinting]
    reviewers: [domain-reviewer, ux-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/workflow-maps.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Draw to-be flows with failure branches"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s3-draw-to-be-flows-with-failure-branches
    skills: [user-flow-diagram, human-in-the-loop, design-thinking]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer, ai-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer]
    output: "docs/ux-flow.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s4
    do: "Wireframe the key steps"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s4-wireframe-the-key-steps
    skills: [wireframing]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/wireframes.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Flows complete and true to the work?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Gaps or wrong process → redraw": s3
gate: "Flow review"
criteria:
  - "Every requirement on a flow step"
  - "Every failure branch ends somewhere visible"
checks:
  - "Domain-expert walkthrough"
on_failure:
  - "Walk every step with an engineer asking 'what if this fails?'"
  - "Re-check against the workflow maps and session notes"
rework: "Review gaps → redraw the affected flow"
outputs:
  - "docs/ux-flow.md"
  - "docs/wireframes.md"
handoff: "UX flows & wireframes → 3.1.2 Prototype & Validate with Users"
learning:
  - "Flow changes found later in usability testing — learning log"
```

# Workflow 3.1.2.1 · Run a Usability Round

Test the prototype with representative users against thresholds set beforehand, fix what fails and retest until it passes.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-1-2-1-usability-round.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-1-2-1-run-usability-round`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-1-2-1-usability-round
title: "Run a Usability Round"
owner: "UX researcher"
inputs:
  - "docs/ux-flow.md"
  - "docs/wireframes.md"
  - "docs/participant-list.md"
preconditions:
  - "Flows agreed"
  - "Participants booked with consent"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Write questions, tasks & thresholds"
    owner: "UX researcher"

    skills: [usability-testing]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer, challenger]
    output: "docs/usability-test-plan.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Build the prototype"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s2-build-the-prototype
    skills: [clickable-prototype, design-thinking, heuristic-evaluation]
    reviewers: [ai-reviewer, privacy-reviewer]
    output: "docs/prototype.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Run moderated sessions"
    owner: "UX researcher"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s3-run-moderated-sessions
    skills: [think-aloud]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer, privacy-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/session-notes.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s4
    do: "Rate findings by severity"
    owner: "UX researcher"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s4-rate-findings-by-severity
    skills: [design-critique]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/usability-findings.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Thresholds met, no severity 1–2 open?"
    owner: "Product owner"

    branches:
      "yes": s5
      "Missed → change prototype & retest": s2
      "Requirement itself wrong → product owner": authority

    do: "Record the validated prototype"

    output: "docs/prototype.md"

  - "Median time on task within target"
  - "No flagged line approved unchecked"

  - "Bias review of tasks"
  - "Second observer"
on_failure:
  - "Add a round"
  - "Drop fidelity back to wireframes"
rework: "Missed thresholds → change the prototype and retest only the failed tasks"
outputs:
  - "docs/usability-test-plan.md"
  - "docs/usability-findings.md"
  - "docs/prototype.md"
handoff: "Validated prototype & usability findings → 3.1.3 Specify UI & States"
learning:
  - "Findings that surprised the team — learning log"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act III DESIGN · Scale: Enterprise. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
DESIGN is part of the **Discovery track** — Are we building the right thing? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## DESIGN: Decide the experience, domain, architecture, data and safeguards — to the depth the risk demands — so that building is low-risk and traceable.
- **3.1 Experience Design** — gate: Experience Review. Produces: UX flows, Validated prototype, Usability findings, UI specification, State matrix, Accessibility checklist.
- **3.2 Domain Modelling** — gate: Domain Model Review. Produces: Ubiquitous language glossary, Context map, Domain model, Invariant catalogue.
- **3.3 Architecture Definition** — gate: Architecture Baseline. Produces: Architecture Impact Check, System design, ADRs, Architecture views, Architecture baseline.
- **3.4 Data Design** — gate: Data Design Review. Produces: Data model, Data ownership table, Data lineage map, Data classification & retention schedule, Migration plan.
- **3.5 Security & Privacy by Design** — gate: Security & Privacy Review. Produces: Threat model, Security requirements, Privacy impact assessment, Vendor security assessment.
- **3.6 Quality Attribute Specification** — gate: Design Readiness. Produces: Ranked quality drivers, Quality-attribute scenarios, Trade-off analysis, Fitness functions, Design readiness record, Design pack, Ready stories, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Design Readiness** — decided by: The architect decides design readiness; the product owner approves Ready stories; the design authority settles cross-team conflicts; no one approves what they authored..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: UXF → PRT → UIS → DOM → ARC → ADR → DAT → THR → DPIA → QAS → DRR → STY → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `design-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Enterprise
Use formal language and our approved templates. Back every claim with a reference to its evidence for audit, flag compliance, security and privacy implications, name the approver for each decision, and keep confidential details out of anything meant for wider sharing.
Access: Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.
enterprise.GUARDRAILS.md:
# Guardrails & hooks — Design

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Enterprise
- Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.
- Watch for: Pasting confidential or personal data into unapproved tools
- Watch for: Agent output in audited artifacts without a human reviewer named

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### DESIGN
- No story enters a sprint without passing the Ready Gate
- Reviewers never approve what they authored
- Design depth is proportional to risk and recorded impact
- Privacy and accessibility by default
- ERP import API only
- Vendor X connector timeline
- Budget and dates from the commitment

### 3.1 Experience Design
- No screens before the flow is agreed
- Never colour alone
- Accessibility policy
- Research ethics & privacy
- Clerks' time away from orders
- Design system

### 3.1.1 Map Journeys & UX Flows
- No screens before the flow is agreed
- Design work traces to requirement IDs
- Release scope
- ERP import API only

### 3.1.2 Prototype & Validate with Users
- Consent before recording
- No moving the thresholds after the round
- Research ethics & privacy
- Clerks' time away from orders
- Consent and anonymised sample data

### 3.1.3 Specify UI & States
- The UI never claims something is done before the system has done it
- Design-system first
- Design system
- Architecture's real async behaviour

### 3.1.4 Design for Accessibility
- Never colour alone
- Every action available by keyboard
- Accessibility policy; EN 301 549 where it applies
- WCAG 2.2 AA minimum
- Design system capabilities

### 3.2 Domain Modelling
- Use the domain's words in UI, code and tests
- Glossary is the single source of terms
- Existing ERP boundaries
- Experts' time

### 3.2.1 Explore the Domain & Ubiquitous Language
- Use the experts' words, not ours
- Glossary is the single source of terms for UI, code and tests
- Experts' time

### 3.2.2 Define Bounded Contexts & Context Map
- No context shared by two owners
- Team boundaries follow context boundaries where possible
- Existing ERP boundaries
- Team structure

### 3.2.3 Model Entities, Aggregates & Lifecycles
- Reference other aggregates by ID only
- Model kept in the architecture repository next to the code
- Context boundaries

### 3.2.4 Specify Invariants & Business Rules

- Rules have named business owners

### 3.3 Architecture Definition
- No story is Ready with an unassessed impact or a draft ADR
- Accepted ADRs are superseded, never edited
- Architecture is updated before implementation, not after
- ERP import API only
- EU data residency
- Vendor X contract

### 3.3.1 Run the Architecture Impact Check
- No story is Ready with an unassessed impact
- 'No impact' is a real answer and should be common
- A current baseline must exist

### 3.3.2 Write the System Design
- No network call inside a transaction
- Retries only with an idempotency key
- Designs are linked from the stories they unblock
- ERP import API only
- Vendor X contract

### 3.3.3 Decide & Record (ADRs)
- Accepted ADRs are never edited — they are superseded
- Agent-drafted ADRs say so and are accepted by a named person
- Commitment conditions
- Budget

### 3.3.4 Describe Views & Update the Baseline
- Reviewer is not the author
- Architecture updated before implementation, not after
- Baseline stored where engineers work
- EU data residency

### 3.4 Data Design
- A transaction spans only owned data and never contains a network call
- No personal data without a purpose and a retention period
- Contracts are versioned
- Record of processing kept current
- ERP owns orders and master data
- Tax retention duties

### 3.4.1 Design the Data Model
- A transaction spans only data the module owns and never contains a network call
- Names follow the glossary
- Database platform
- Load model

### 3.4.2 Assign Ownership, Consistency & Contracts
- Two owners for one entity is always a finding
- Contracts are versioned
- ERP owns orders and master data

### 3.4.3 Map Lineage, Classification & Retention
- No personal data without a purpose and a retention period
- Record of processing kept current
- Tax retention duties
- GDPR

### 3.4.4 Plan Migration & Backfill
- Structure change and read switch never in the same release
- Cut-over follows the rollout by site
- Business calendar
- Rollback window

### 3.5 Security & Privacy by Design
- Least privilege for every service account
- No personal data to a supplier without a DPA
- Privacy by design and by default
- Threat models updated on every architecture change
- GDPR
- Supplier contracts
- Identity platform

### 3.5.1 Model Threats (STRIDE)
- Workers never inherit user authority; re-authorise at the point of effect
- Threat models updated on every architecture change
- Internet-facing mailbox
- ERP integration rights

### 3.5.2 Define Security Requirements & Controls
- Least privilege for every service account
- Secrets never in code or config files
- Identity platform capabilities

### 3.5.3 Assess Privacy Impact (DPIA)
- No processing of personal data without a lawful basis
- Privacy by design and by default
- GDPR
- Contracts with customers

### 3.5.4 Assess Third-Party & Supply-Chain Risk
- No personal data to a supplier without a DPA
- Supplier policy aligned to ISO/IEC 27036
- Connector timeline
- Budget

### 3.6 Quality Attribute Specification
- No NFR without a number and a verification method
- No story enters a sprint without passing the Ready Gate
- Fitness functions run in the pipeline or in production
- Gate failures and corrections recorded as evidence
- Measured baselines
- Sprint cadence

### 3.6.1 Identify & Rank Quality Drivers
- Everything cannot be the priority
- Drivers recorded in the baseline
- Budget and timeline from the commitment

### 3.6.2 Write Measurable Quality-Attribute Scenarios
- No NFR without a number and a verification method
- Scenarios trace to requirements
- Measured baselines

### 3.6.3 Analyse Trade-offs & Fitness Functions
- A trade-off is accepted by the owner of the affected measure
- Fitness functions run in the pipeline or in production
- Pipeline capacity for checks

### 3.6.4 Run Design Readiness & Make Stories Ready
- No story enters a sprint without passing the Ready Gate
- Gate failures and corrections are recorded as evidence
- Sprint cadence

enterprise.workflows/design-3-1-1-1-map-flows.md:
# Workflow 3.1.1.1 · Map the To-Be Flows

Turn the release's requirements and today's workflow into agreed to-be flows and wireframes, including what happens when things fail.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-1-1-1-map-flows.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-1-1-1-run-map-flows`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-1-1-1-map-flows
title: "Map the To-Be Flows"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/workflow-maps.md"
  - "docs/jtbd.md"
preconditions:
  - "Requirements baseline approved"
  - "Release scope known from the roadmap"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Select jobs & requirements for the release"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s1-select-jobs-and-requirements-for-the-release
    skills: [double-diamond]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Policy change needed → process owner": authority
      "No user-facing change": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Analyse today's task"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s2-analyse-today-s-task
    skills: [task-analysis, journey-mapping, service-blueprinting]
    reviewers: [domain-reviewer, ux-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/workflow-maps.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Draw to-be flows with failure branches"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s3-draw-to-be-flows-with-failure-branches
    skills: [user-flow-diagram, human-in-the-loop, design-thinking]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer, ai-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer]
    output: "docs/ux-flow.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s4
    do: "Wireframe the key steps"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s4-wireframe-the-key-steps
    skills: [wireframing]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/wireframes.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Flows complete and true to the work?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Gaps or wrong process → redraw": s3
gate: "Flow review"
criteria:
  - "Every requirement on a flow step"
  - "Every failure branch ends somewhere visible"
checks:
  - "Domain-expert walkthrough"
on_failure:
  - "Walk every step with an engineer asking 'what if this fails?'"
  - "Re-check against the workflow maps and session notes"
rework: "Review gaps → redraw the affected flow"
outputs:
  - "docs/ux-flow.md"
  - "docs/wireframes.md"
handoff: "UX flows & wireframes → 3.1.2 Prototype & Validate with Users"
learning:
  - "Flow changes found later in usability testing — learning log"
```
enterprise.workflows/design-3-1-2-1-usability-round:
# Workflow 3.1.2.1 · Run a Usability Round

Test the prototype with representative users against thresholds set beforehand, fix what fails and retest until it passes.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-1-2-1-usability-round.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-1-2-1-run-usability-round`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-1-2-1-usability-round
title: "Run a Usability Round"
owner: "UX researcher"
inputs:
  - "docs/ux-flow.md"
  - "docs/wireframes.md"
  - "docs/participant-list.md"
preconditions:
  - "Flows agreed"
  - "Participants booked with consent"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Write questions, tasks & thresholds"
    owner: "UX researcher"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s1-write-questions-tasks-and-thresholds
    skills: [usability-testing]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer, challenger]
    output: "docs/usability-test-plan.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Build the prototype"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s2-build-the-prototype
    skills: [clickable-prototype, design-thinking, heuristic-evaluation]
    reviewers: [ai-reviewer, privacy-reviewer]
    output: "docs/prototype.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Run moderated sessions"
    owner: "UX researcher"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s3-run-moderated-sessions
    skills: [think-aloud]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer, privacy-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/session-notes.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s4
    do: "Rate findings by severity"
    owner: "UX researcher"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s4-rate-findings-by-severity
    skills: [design-critique]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/usability-findings.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Thresholds met, no severity 1–2 open?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s5
      "Missed → change prototype & retest": s2
      "Requirement itself wrong → product owner": authority
      "Concept rejected → back to PLAN": stop
  - id: s5
    do: "Record the validated prototype"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s5-record-the-validated-prototype
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/prototype.md"
    checkpoint: review
gate: "Prototype validation"
criteria:
  - "Task success ≥ 5/6"
  - "Median time on task within target"
  - "No flagged line approved unchecked"
checks:
  - "Bias review of tasks"
  - "Second observer"
on_failure:
  - "Add a round"
  - "Drop fidelity back to wireframes"
rework: "Missed thresholds → change the prototype and retest only the failed tasks"
outputs:
  - "docs/usability-test-plan.md"
  - "docs/usability-findings.md"
  - "docs/prototype.md"
handoff: "Validated prototype & usability findings → 3.1.3 Specify UI & States"
learning:
  - "Findings that surprised the team — learning log"
```

```yaml
title: "Specify Screens & States"
owner: "Designer"
inputs:

  - "docs/usability-findings.md"
  - "docs/system-design.md"
preconditions:

steps:

  - id: s2

    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-3-1-s2-compose-from-design-system-components
    skills: [atomic-design, design-system]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer]
    output: "docs/ui-spec.md"

  - id: s3
```

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-1-4-1-a11y-review.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-1-4-1-run-a11y-review`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-1-4-1-a11y-review
title: "Review the Design for Accessibility"
owner: "Designer"
inputs:
  - "docs/ui-spec.md"
  - "docs/prototype.md"
preconditions:
  - "UI spec drafted"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Select criteria per component"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

  - id: s3

    decision: "All applicable criteria pass?"

on_failure:
  - "Add the manual walkthroughs"
rework: "Failed criterion → redesign the component and recheck only it"

  - "docs/ui-spec.md"

learning:
  - "Accessibility defects found later — learning log"
```

# Workflow 3.6.4.2 · Run the Ready Gate on a Story

Run the eight conditions — purpose, requirements, acceptance criteria, dependencies, architecture impact, design, testability, size — on one story, record any failure with its correction, and recheck only what changed.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-6-4-2-ready-gate.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-6-4-2-run-ready-gate`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-6-4-2-ready-gate
title: "Run the Ready Gate on a Story"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"
  - "docs/definition-of-ready.md"
  - "docs/impact-check.md"
  - "docs/ui-spec.md"
preconditions:
  - "Story sliced by behaviour with acceptance criteria"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Check purpose, requirements & criteria (1–3)"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-4-2-s1-check-purpose-requirements-and-criteria-1-3
    skills: [invest, specification-by-example]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, requirements-reviewer]
    output: "docs/backlog-item.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Check dependencies, impact & design (4–6)"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-4-2-s2-check-dependencies-impact-and-design-4-6
    skills: [definition-of-ready, design-review]
    reviewers: [architecture-reviewer, ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/ready-gate-result.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Dependency without an owner → delivery lead": authority
  - id: s3
    do: "Check testability & size (7–8)"
    owner: "QA lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-6-4-2-s3-check-testability-and-size-7-8
    skills: [three-amigos]
    reviewers: [quality-reviewer, engineering-reviewer, researcher]
    output: "docs/ready-gate-result.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "All eight conditions met?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Failed condition → its return point; recheck only what changed": s1
      "Story no longer needed → remove": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Record result, failures & corrections"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

  - "Named approver who is not an author"

  - "docs/ready-gate-result.md"
  - "docs/backlog-item.md"

  - "Which condition fails most often — learning log"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act III DESIGN · Scale: Platform. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
DESIGN is part of the **Discovery track** — Are we building the right thing? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## DESIGN: Decide the experience, domain, architecture, data and safeguards — to the depth the risk demands — so that building is low-risk and traceable.
- **3.1 Experience Design** — gate: Experience Review. Produces: UX flows, Validated prototype, Usability findings, UI specification, State matrix, Accessibility checklist.
- **3.2 Domain Modelling** — gate: Domain Model Review. Produces: Ubiquitous language glossary, Context map, Domain model, Invariant catalogue.
- **3.3 Architecture Definition** — gate: Architecture Baseline. Produces: Architecture Impact Check, System design, ADRs, Architecture views, Architecture baseline.
- **3.4 Data Design** — gate: Data Design Review. Produces: Data model, Data ownership table, Data lineage map, Data classification & retention schedule, Migration plan.
- **3.5 Security & Privacy by Design** — gate: Security & Privacy Review. Produces: Threat model, Security requirements, Privacy impact assessment, Vendor security assessment.
- **3.6 Quality Attribute Specification** — gate: Design Readiness. Produces: Ranked quality drivers, Quality-attribute scenarios, Trade-off analysis, Fitness functions, Design readiness record, Design pack, Ready stories, Learning log.
- Act gate: **Design Readiness** — decided by: The architect decides design readiness; the product owner approves Ready stories; the design authority settles cross-team conflicts; no one approves what they authored..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: UXF → PRT → UIS → DOM → ARC → ADR → DAT → THR → DPIA → QAS → DRR → STY → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `design-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Platform
Treat other internal teams as the customers. Capture their needs as service or API contracts, and consider versioning, backward compatibility, self-service, documentation and adoption.
Access: Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.

# Guardrails & hooks — Design

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Platform
- Read and write the platform repository and API docs in branches; consuming teams' systems are read-only.
- Watch for: Building what the platform team finds interesting, not what consumers need
- Watch for: Breaking changes without versioning

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

# Workflow 3.1.1.1 · Map the To-Be Flows

Turn the release's requirements and today's workflow into agreed to-be flows and wireframes, including what happens when things fail.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-1-1-1-map-flows.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-1-1-1-run-map-flows`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: design-3-1-1-1-map-flows
title: "Map the To-Be Flows"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
  - "docs/workflow-maps.md"
  - "docs/jtbd.md"
preconditions:
  - "Requirements baseline approved"
  - "Release scope known from the roadmap"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Select jobs & requirements for the release"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s1-select-jobs-and-requirements-for-the-release
    skills: [double-diamond]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/requirements-baseline.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Policy change needed → process owner": authority
      "No user-facing change": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Analyse today's task"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s2-analyse-today-s-task
    skills: [task-analysis, journey-mapping, service-blueprinting]
    reviewers: [domain-reviewer, ux-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/workflow-maps.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Draw to-be flows with failure branches"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s3-draw-to-be-flows-with-failure-branches
    skills: [user-flow-diagram, human-in-the-loop, design-thinking]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer, ai-reviewer, accessibility-reviewer]
    output: "docs/ux-flow.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s4
    do: "Wireframe the key steps"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-1-1-s4-wireframe-the-key-steps
    skills: [wireframing]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/wireframes.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Flows complete and true to the work?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": gate
      "Gaps or wrong process → redraw": s3
gate: "Flow review"
criteria:
  - "Every requirement on a flow step"
  - "Every failure branch ends somewhere visible"
checks:
  - "Domain-expert walkthrough"
on_failure:

  - "Re-check against the workflow maps and session notes"
rework: "Review gaps → redraw the affected flow"
outputs:
  - "docs/ux-flow.md"
  - "docs/wireframes.md"
handoff: "UX flows & wireframes → 3.1.2 Prototype & Validate with Users"
learning:
  - "Flow changes found later in usability testing — learning log"
```

# Workflow 3.1.2.1 · Run a Usability Round

Test the prototype with representative users against thresholds set beforehand, fix what fails and retest until it passes.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/design-3-1-2-1-usability-round.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `design-3-1-2-1-run-usability-round`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml

title: "Run a Usability Round"
owner: "UX researcher"
inputs:
  - "docs/ux-flow.md"
  - "docs/wireframes.md"
  - "docs/participant-list.md"
preconditions:
  - "Flows agreed"
  - "Participants booked with consent"
steps:

    do: "Write questions, tasks & thresholds"

    checkpoint: review
  - id: s2
    do: "Build the prototype"
    owner: "Designer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: design-3-1-2-1-s2-build-the-prototype
    skills: [clickable-prototype, design-thinking, heuristic-evaluation]
    reviewers: [ai-reviewer, privacy-reviewer]
    output: "docs/prototype.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3

    output: "docs/session-notes.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s4
    do: "Rate findings by severity"
    owner: "UX researcher"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

    skills: [design-critique]
    reviewers: [ux-reviewer]
    output: "docs/usability-findings.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Thresholds met, no severity 1–2 open?"

  - "Drop fidelity back to wireframes"
rework: "Missed thresholds → change the prototype and retest only the failed tasks"
outputs:
  - "docs/usability-test-plan.md"
  - "docs/usability-findings.md"
  - "docs/prototype.md"
handoff: "Validated prototype & usability findings → 3.1.3 Specify UI & States"

  - "Findings that surprised the team — learning log"
```
